practiceReport.name: DJ Wonnum
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Trench/box position (LB) — historically higher active rate through braced upper-body & ankle soreness (81% baseline).
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: Wonnum was able to practice in a limited capacity Wednesday, but that didn't end up being enough for him to suit up Thursday. He leads the Lions with 7.0 sacks this season, so the veteran defensive end's absence is a big deal for Detroit. Tyler Lacy, Ahmed Hassanein, Eric O'Neill and Anthony Lucas could all be involved in trying to fill the void left by Wonnum's absence Thursday.

practiceReport.name: Chuck Clark
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran starter profile (10th NFL season, 91% snap share) — elevated Questionable active conversion (84%) & Wednesday maintenance tolerance.
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: Clark dealt with a hamstring issue during Week 12 prep and is going to miss his first game of the campaign as a result. He's been a starter at safety for the Lions all season and played every defensive snap in three of Detroit's past four games. Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch will start at safety Thursday, with Andre Cisco working in reserve.

practiceReport.name: D.J. Reed
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran starter profile (9th NFL season, 94% snap share) — elevated Questionable active conversion (84%) & Wednesday maintenance tolerance.
practiceReport.beatComment: Reed appears to be on track to return to action Thursday against the Bears after missing three straight games with a hip injury. The cornerback will have two more chances to officially practice ahead of Week 12.

practiceReport.name: Sam LaPorta
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (89% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
practiceReport.beatComment: Now that he's gotten a full practice under his belt this week, LaPorta should be in the clear for Thursday's game against the Bears. The fourth-year tight end is coming off a three-catch, 62-yard performance on six targets in a 31-21 win over the Buccaneers this past Sunday, with the yardage and target totals both representing his highest marks since the Lions' Week 6 bye.

practiceReport.name: Khalil Dorsey
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (CB) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Dorsey hurt his wrist early in Sunday's game and was initially deemed questionable to return. The veteran cornerback has since been able to re-enter the game, albeit with a club over the hand that he injured. Dorsey has been working in a rotational role at cornerback, logging a defensive snap share between 32 and 38 percent three straight weeks.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Skyler Gill-Howard
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Gill-Howard suffered a season-ending knee injury during the Lions' Week 11 win over the Buccaneers. The rookie sixth-rounder will finish his first NFL campaign with 11 tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, across 10 regular-season games.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Ben Bartch
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 6 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Bartch has already missed three games due to a foot injury that he sustained against the Bills in Week 2. While on IR, he'll be forced to miss at least four games, so Week 11 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Nov. 22, is the earliest he can return.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Devin White
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 6 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: White was diagnosed with a broken forearm following the Lions' Week 5 win over the Cardinals. He'll be required to miss at least the next four games on IR, and while he's likely to be sidelined past that minimum window, there's optimism that the veteran linebacker will return at some point this season. Malcolm Rodriguez is the next man up at linebacker in White's absence.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Giovanni Manu
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Manu continues to recover from a knee injury he sustained in October of 2025. He's required to miss at least the first four games of the regular season, meaning the earliest he can return is Week 5 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Oct. 11.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jack Campbell
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Campbell suffered a neck injury while making a tackle in the third quarter of last Sunday's win over Minnesota and remains in the hospital. Detroit head coach Dan Campbell shared Friday that the linebacker continues to improve, but his placement on IR means he'll miss at least the team's next four games. K.J. Britt, who Detroit signed off New England's practice squad Wednesday, may be asked to immediately step into a starting role.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Cade Mays
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Mays missed the Lions' two prior games due to an ankle injury that he sustained against the Vikings in Week 8. His placement on IR means he's required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against Minnesota. Juice Scruggs figures to be the Lions' starting center for as long as Mays is sidelined.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Isiah Pacheco
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Pacheco has been sidelined for the entirety of the regular season to this point after undergoing back surgery in September. Sione Vaki has been working as the Lions' clear RB2, though Jahmyr Gibbs has been a true workhorse out of the backfield. If Pacheco does return at the end of the regular season, it's hard to envision him having a big impact coming off back surgery.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Aidan Hutchinson
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Hutchinson's move to IR was merely a formality after he was diagnosed with a torn ACL in his right knee following his early exit from this past Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. The No. 2 overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft has now succumbed to two season-ending injuries through his first five years in the league, after a fractured tibia and fibula in his left leg cut short his 2024 campaign.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Avonte Maddox
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Maddox will miss the rest of the 2026 season due to a left foot injury he sustained in the Lions' Week 2 loss to the Bills. He'll shift his focus toward being fully healthy for the 2027 campaign, though he'll enter the offseason as an unrestricted free agent. With Maddox, Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (knee) all sidelined, Thomas Harper and Chuck Clark will serve as Detroit's starting safeties for the time being.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Damone Clark
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: It's not immediately clear what kind of injury Clark suffered, but the timing of the transaction means he's now in line to spend the entire 2026 season on IR unless he works out an injury settlement with the Lions. His departure could open up more opportunities for fellow free-agent acquisition Amen Ogbongbemiga.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jimmy Rolder
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: This move was anticipated, as Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury in the Lions' win over Minnesota on Sunday. The rookie linebacker logged a career-high 17 defensive snaps and notched his first NFL sack in that contest, so his injury comes at an unfortunate time. Rolder will now turn his focus toward rehabbing the injury in order to be ready for offseason activities in 2027.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Kendrick Law
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Placed on Injured Reserve (Knee - ACL) on Jul 22, 2026; ineligible to return in 2026 under NFL CBA rules.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Payton Turner
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026

irAndReserveTracker.name: Tom Kennedy
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Kennedy suffered a season-ending MCL injury in his right knee during the Lions' Week 5 win over the Cardinals. His move to IR opens a spot on Detroit's 53-man roster, and in his absence, Jacob Saylors is in line to take over return duties on kickoffs and punts.
